samples.name: h264_high444_profile
samples.description: Test H.264 High444 profile encoding Decoder round-trip validation is DISABLED for this sample: NVDEC has no H.264 4:4:4 decode, so the decode capability query correctly returns VK_ERROR_VIDEO_PROFILE_FORMAT_NOT_SUPPORTED_KHR and the round-trip can never succeed. The ENCODE itself is still exercised and checked; only the decode-back step is skipped. Validate the bitstream with a software decoder if stronger checking is wanted.

samples.name: av1_high_profile
samples.description: NEGATIVE CELL. AV1 High profile (stdProfile 1). NVENC encodes AV1 Main (profile 0) only -- High requires 4:4:4 and Professional 4:2:2/12-bit, neither of which the AV1 encoder implements on any shipping chip -- so the capability query must reject it. Scoring the cell as a plain N/S instead would be a soft outcome: an N/S and a silently-accepted profile are both non-failures, so a driver that started accepting AV1 High would turn the cell green rather than red. PORTABILITY: this cell asserts NVIDIA hardware behaviour. On an implementation that genuinely supports this profile the cell will fail; that failure is the correct signal to look, and the fix is a skip-list entry scoped to that driver, not deleting the cell.

samples.name: av1_professional_profile
samples.description: NEGATIVE CELL. AV1 Professional profile (stdProfile 2). Same reasoning as av1_high_profile: NVENC encodes AV1 Main only, so the capability query must reject this. A plain N/S cannot distinguish a correct rejection from a profile the driver has started accepting, which is why this cell asserts the rejection itself. PORTABILITY: this cell asserts NVIDIA hardware behaviour. On an implementation that genuinely supports this profile the cell will fail; that failure is the correct signal to look, and the fix is a skip-list entry scoped to that driver, not deleting the cell.

samples.name: h265_12bit_unsupported
samples.description: NEGATIVE CELL. HEVC 12-bit 4:2:0 encode. The driver advertises 12-bit under __VK_VIDEO_DECODE_USAGE_MASK only -- NVENC has no 12-bit encode on any shipping chip -- so vkGetPhysicalDeviceVideoCapabilitiesKHR must reject the profile. Decode at 12-bit is supported and covered by four positive cells in decode_samples.json; this cell keeps the encode half of that asymmetry measured, so 12-bit encode quietly starting to 'work' (and producing garbage, or silently downshifting to 10-bit) is a test failure and not a silence. The cell drives an ENCODE_H265 / 420 / 12-bit / FORMAT_RANGE_EXTENSIONS profile and passes only when the query returns VK_ERROR_VIDEO_PROFILE_FORMAT_NOT_SUPPORTED_KHR and the app exits 69. SOURCE: scripts/gen_negative_test_content.sh. PORTABILITY: this cell asserts NVIDIA hardware behaviour. On an implementation that genuinely supports this profile the cell will fail; that failure is the correct signal to look, and the fix is a skip-list entry scoped to that driver, not deleting the cell. Integrity is enforced by the generator's own gates (exact byte count, an ffprobe profile/pix_fmt check, and for the 12-bit input a peak sample above the 10-bit range) rather than by source_checksum: the artifact is re-encoded locally, so its bytes depend on the ffmpeg/x264 build and a hash would fail on a version difference while saying nothing about whether the format is right.
